title: Sampling isometric tensor network states with monitored quantum circuits
authors: Yuqing Rong, Huan-Hai Zhou, Guo-Yi Zhu, Jinguo Liu
abstract: Projected entangled pair states (PEPS) provide an efficient variational ansatz for two-dimensional quantum phases, but computing observables remains challenging because PEPS contraction is generally costly.   Here, we parameterize two-dimensional quantum states using variational PEPS subject to isometric constraints and map the resulting ansatz onto monitored quantum circuits, replacing tensor-network contraction with circuit sampling.   For infinite cylinders, the transfer matrix defines a quantum channel on the virtual boundary. We use a fixed-point treatment and a monitored-circuit unraveling of this channel to evaluate observables efficiently.   Using a constant number of variational parameters and a number of qubits that scales only with the cylinder width, our method yields a phase diagram for the $J_1$-$J_2$ model in qualitative agreement with DMRG results.   Because the monitored circuits are compatible with near-term quantum hardware, this approach provides a hybrid quantum-classical framework for simulating two-dimensional quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper develops a novel hybrid quantum-classical approach to simulate 2D quantum many-body systems using isometric tensor networks (isoPEPS). It replaces complex tensor contractions with sampling from monitored quantum circuits, making the simulation compatible with near-term quantum hardware. The method successfully estimates ground-state properties for models like the J1-J2 Heisenberg model, validating its potential for simulating complex quantum phases.
main_problem: The primary challenge is efficiently computing observables for two-dimensional quantum lattice models whose exact Hilbert space dimension grows exponentially.
main_result: The proposed method successfully estimates the energy density for the J1-J2 model and TFIM in qualitative agreement with established methods like DMRG, demonstrating a viable hybrid quantum-classical simulation framework.
method: The authors parameterize the quantum state using isometric tensor networks (isoPEPS) and replace costly tensor-network contraction with sampling from monitored quantum circuits.
model_or_system: The study focuses on 2D quantum spin systems, specifically the J1-J2 Heisenberg model and the Transverse-Field Ising Model (TFIM), implemented on an infinite cylindrical spiral geometry.
key_observables: Energy density, correlation length ($\xi$), longitudinal and transverse magnetizations ($|\langle Z angle|, |\langle X angle|$), and real-space spin correlations ($\langle S_i \cdot S_j angle$).
important_parameters: The ratio $J_2/J_1$ for the Heisenberg model, and the transverse field strength $g$ for the TFIM.
main_assumptions: The method assumes standard ergodicity for the time average to converge to the stationary boundary state, and the optimization relies on sampling noisy energy estimators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the variational sampling framework, the circuit structure for monitoring, the comparison of energy densities against DMRG, and the extraction of correlation lengths and magnetizations for the TFIM.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the isoPEPS ansatz, details the mapping onto monitored quantum circuits for cylindrical/spiral geometries, presents the sampling and optimization procedure (using CMA-ES), and validates the method by calculating observables for the TFIM and J1-J2 model.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the computational bottleneck in simulating 2D quantum matter by translating the intractable tensor contraction into a physically realizable, near-term quantum circuit sampling routine.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Variational sampling framework for isoPEPS. (a) An isoPEPS on an infinite cylinder, represented in a spiral geometry with W sites around the circumference. Each site carries a rank-five PEPS tensor with four virtual legs—one incoming and one outgoing leg along each of the horizontal (hi) and spiral (v) directions—and one physical leg p. The arrows specify the isometric orientation: the two incoming virtual indices are mapped to the physical index and the two outgoing virtual indices. The |0⟩line is an ancillary input introduced in the unitary circuit representation, rather than an additional leg of the PEPS tensor. (b) The local isometric tensor is embedded in a three-qubit...

Figure 2: TFIM energy benchmark on a 3 × ∞cylinder. (a) Energy density of the D = 2, p = 3 isoPEPS after sampling-based optimization, evaluated by exact tensor-network contraction, compared with DMRG on the same W = 3 cylinder. (b) Relative deviation of the exact-contraction isoPEPS energy from the DMRG result, |EisoPEPS −EDMRG|/|EDMRG|. The deviation peaks near the square- lattice quantum critical point gc = 3.04438(2) [38].

Figure 3: Optimization history for the J1-J2 Heisenberg model at J2/J1 = 0.5. IsoPEPS with W = 4, D = 2, p = 3, and a 2 × 2 unit cell (72 parameters). Each energy estimate uses 40,000 single-site measurement samples from the monitored trajectory.

Figure 4: Magnetic and dimer order calculated for the J1-J2 Heisenberg model. Magnetic order parameters at the N´eel wavevector M 2(π, π) and the stripe wavevector M 2(0, π), together with the vertical-bond dimer order parameter M2 D(0, π), as a function of J2/J1. Colors denote the three observables; solid (dashed) curves show the D = 2 isoPEPS (DMRG) results. The shaded labels mark the N´eel, VBS, and stripe regimes: M2(π, π) dominates at small J2/J1, M 2 D(0, π) peaks in the intermediate window J2/J1 ≈0.5–0.6, and M 2(0, π) takes over at larger J2/J1.

Figure 5: Momentum-resolved spin and dimer structure factors for the J1–J2 Heisenberg model. (Top row) Spin structure factor S(q) at J2/J1 = 0.0, 0.5, 0.6, 1.0: a N´eel peak at (π, π) for J2/J1 = 0.0, suppressed in the intermediate window, and shifted to the stripe wavevector (0, π) at J2/J1 = 1.0. (Bottom row) Vertical-bond dimer structure factor Sy D(q) at the same four couplings: a peak at (0, π) for J2/J1 = 0.5, 0.6, consistent with the columnar-VBS signal in Fig. 4, and featureless at J2/J1 = 0.0, 1.0. The dense qy sampling in the plots is used only for display; the W = 4 cylinder admits the four transverse crystal momenta qy ∈{0, π/2, π, 3π/2}.
